questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Preamble has been amended only once, by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
2. In the Berubari Union case the Supreme Court held the Preamble to be a part of the Constitution.
3. In the Kesavananda Bharati case the Supreme Court held the Preamble to be a part of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' and is the only amendment to the Preamble. In Berubari (1960) the Court said the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution; Kesavananda (1973) reversed this and held it is a part.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 5 to 11 in Part II of the Constitution deal with citizenship.
2. Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
3. The Constitution itself lays down the modes of loss of citizenship after its commencement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Part II (Arts 5-11) identifies citizens at the commencement of the Constitution, and Art 11 gives Parliament the power to legislate. Acquisition and loss thereafter are governed by the Citizenship Act, 1955, not the Constitution, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The protection under Article 20 (against conviction for offences) cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency.
Statement-II: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act provided that the right to move the court for enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended during an Emergency.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Before 1978 all fundamental rights enforcement could be suspended under Art 359. The 44th Amendment (1978) carved out Arts 20 and 21, which is exactly why Art 20 protection survives an Emergency.

questions.q: Which one of the following Directive Principles of State Policy was inserted by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011?
o: Equal justice and free legal aid
Participation of workers in the management of industries
Protection and improvement of the environment
questions.e: Art 43B (cooperative societies) came with the 97th Amendment, which also made the right to form cooperatives a fundamental right under Art 19(1)(c). Arts 39A, 43A and 48A were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fundamental Duties were incorporated by the 42nd Amendment Act on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
2. Part IVA of the Constitution contains only one Article, Article 51A.
3. Fundamental Duties are justiciable and can be enforced through writs under Article 32.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Part IVA has only Art 51A, added in 1976 on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice. The Duties are non-justiciable, like the Directive Principles, so no writ lies for their enforcement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The President can promulgate an Ordinance only when either House of Parliament is not in session.
2. An Ordinance has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament.
3. The President can amend the Constitution through an Ordinance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Art 123 an Ordinance can be issued when either House is not in session and has the force of an Act. Because it is an executive-legislative power limited to ordinary legislation, it cannot be used to amend the Constitution.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
2. The Rajya Sabha has the power to amend a Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha.
3. The decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Arts 109 and 110 restrict Money Bills to the Lok Sabha and make the Speaker's certificate final. The Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject.

questions.q: Which one of the following writs can be issued against a private individual in appropriate cases?
questions.e: Habeas corpus tests the legality of detention and can lie against private persons who illegally detain someone. Mandamus, prohibition and certiorari are directed at public authorities or judicial and quasi-judicial bodies.
questions.u: Supreme Court, High Court & Subordinate Courts

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Part IX of the Constitution deals with Panchayats and covers Articles 243 to 243-O.
2. The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats.
3. The Twelfth Schedule lists 29 subjects for Municipalities.
4. The State Election Commission superintends the conduct of Panchayat elections.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment inserted Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects) and gave election control to the State Election Commission (Art 243K). The Twelfth Schedule, added by the 74th Amendment, lists 18 subjects, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.e: NITI Aayog was set up in 2015 by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet. The Finance Commission (Art 280), UPSC (Art 315) and Election Commission (Art 324) derive their existence from the Constitution.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510.
2. Francisco de Almeida advocated the 'Blue Water Policy' of Portuguese naval supremacy.
3. Albuquerque shifted the Portuguese capital in India from Cochin to Goa in 1530.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Albuquerque took Goa in 1510 and Almeida stressed command of the seas over land territory. The capital shifted from Cochin to Goa in 1530 under Nino da Cunha, long after Albuquerque's death in 1515, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Permanent Settlement of Bengal : Lord Cornwallis
2. Subsidiary Alliance (first accepted by the Nizam of Hyderabad) : Lord Wellesley
3. Doctrine of Lapse : Lord Wellesley
4. Vernacular Press Act : Lord Lytton
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Cornwallis (1793), Wellesley (Subsidiary Alliance, Hyderabad 1798) and Lytton (Vernacular Press Act, 1878) are correct. The Doctrine of Lapse is associated with Lord Dalhousie, not Wellesley.
questions.s: Spectrum, Expansion and Consolidation of British Power

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of organisation and founder/leader is NOT correctly matched?
o: Atmiya Sabha : Raja Ram Mohan Roy
Servants of India Society : Gopal Krishna Gokhale
questions.e: The Social Service League (1911) was founded by N. M. Joshi; Behramji Malabari is associated with Seva Sadan. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Surat Split of the Indian National Congress
2. Formation of the All India Muslim League
3. Morley-Minto Reforms
4. Lucknow Pact between the Congress and the Muslim League
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Muslim League was formed in 1906, the Congress split at Surat in 1907, the Morley-Minto Reforms followed in 1909, and the two parties came together in the Lucknow Pact of 1916.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kheda was Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India.
2. In the Ahmedabad mill workers' dispute Gandhi undertook a fast for the first time in an Indian movement.
3. The Champaran Satyagraha was directed against the tinkathia system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Champaran (1917) was the first Satyagraha in India, against the tinkathia system of compulsory indigo cultivation on part of the holding. Kheda (1918) came later, so statement 1 is wrong; the Ahmedabad fast (1918) was his first hunger strike in India.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q: Under the Poona Pact of 1932, the number of seats reserved for the Depressed Classes in the provincial legislatures was increased, compared with the Communal Award, from 71 to
questions.e: The Communal Award of 1932 had given 71 reserved seats with separate electorates. After Gandhi's fast, the Poona Pact replaced separate electorates with joint electorates and raised the reserved seats to 148.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced it at the Centre.
2. The Act provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
3. The all-India federation envisaged by the Act came into operation in 1937.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Provincial autonomy replaced provincial dyarchy, which was shifted to the Centre, and a Federal Court was set up in 1937. The federation never came into being because the required number of princely states did not join, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Major Rock Edict XIII describes Ashoka's remorse after the Kalinga war.
2. All the inscriptions of Ashoka were written in the Brahmi script.
3. The edicts at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra were inscribed in the Kharosthi script.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rock Edict XIII records the Kalinga war and Ashoka's turn to dhamma, and the north-western edicts use Kharosthi. Ashoka's inscriptions also appear in Greek and Aramaic in Afghanistan, so 'all in Brahmi' is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Iltutmish : Silver tanka and copper jital
Alauddin Khalji : Dagh and Chehra system
questions.e: Diwan-i-Khairat, the department of charity, was set up by Firuz Shah Tughlaq. Balban is known for the Diwan-i-Arz reorganisation and the court rituals of Sijda and Paibos.

questions.q: The Sun Temple at Konark in Odisha was built by a ruler of which one of the following dynasties?
questions.e: The Konark Sun Temple, in the Kalinga style of Nagara architecture, was built by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty in the 13th century. The Chandelas built Khajuraho, the Rashtrakutas the Kailasa temple at Ellora and the Solankis the Sun Temple at Modhera.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania, Indian Art and Culture

questions.q: Which one of the following seismic discontinuities separates the outer core from the inner core of the Earth?
questions.e: The Lehmann discontinuity lies at the boundary of the liquid outer core and the solid inner core. Mohorovicic separates crust from mantle, Gutenberg separates mantle from outer core, and Conrad lies within the continental crust between upper and lower layers.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Marble is formed by the metamorphism of limestone.
2. Quartzite is formed by the metamorphism of sandstone.
3. Slate is formed by the metamorphism of sandstone.
4. Gneiss can be formed by the metamorphism of granite.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Marble (from limestone), quartzite (from sandstone) and gneiss (from granite) are standard metamorphic transformations. Slate forms from shale or clay, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 5

questions.q:
Which of the following ocean currents are cold currents?
1. Labrador Current
2. Benguela Current
3. Agulhas Current
4. Kuroshio Current
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The Labrador and Benguela currents carry cold water towards the equator along continental west or north-east coasts. The Agulhas and Kuroshio currents carry warm tropical water poleward along western ocean margins.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 14

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Fresh snow has a higher albedo than forests.
2. The Earth is at perihelion in early July.
3. Most of the atmospheric ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Bright snow reflects far more sunlight than dark forest, and ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere. Perihelion is around 3 January; the Earth is at aphelion in early July, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 8

questions.q:
Statement-I: The westerlies are much stronger and more persistent in the Southern Hemisphere than in the Northern Hemisphere.
Statement-II: The Southern Hemisphere in the mid-latitudes has vast stretches of ocean with very little land to obstruct the winds.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Land masses create friction and pressure disturbances that weaken winds in the Northern Hemisphere. In the south, the open ocean allows steady flow, giving rise to the 'Roaring Forties', 'Furious Fifties' and 'Shrieking Sixties'.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 10

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Pir Panjal is the longest range of the Lesser Himalaya.
2. The longitudinal valleys called 'duns' lie between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks.
3. The Karewa deposits of the Kashmir Valley are lacustrine in origin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Pir Panjal is the longest and most prominent Lesser Himalayan range. Duns such as Dehradun lie between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks, and Karewas are lake deposits left when the ancient Kashmir lake drained.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Son : Right bank tributary of the Ganga
2. Gandak : Left bank tributary of the Ganga
3. Chambal : Right bank tributary of the Yamuna
4. Kosi : Right bank tributary of the Ganga
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Son comes from the peninsular side (right bank) while the Gandak, from the Nepal Himalaya, is a left bank tributary. The Chambal joins the Yamuna from the right. The Kosi also comes from the Himalaya and joins on the left bank, so pair 4 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 3

questions.q: Which one of the following soils is formed by intense leaching under conditions of high temperature and heavy rainfall with alternate wet and dry seasons?
questions.e: Heavy rain washes away silica and bases, leaving iron and aluminium oxides, which form laterite. It is therefore poor in nitrogen, potash and lime and typical of the Western Ghats, Meghalaya and parts of the Eastern Ghats.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI India: Physical Environment, Ch 6

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gross National Product is equal to Gross Domestic Product plus net factor income from abroad.
2. Net National Product at factor cost is called National Income.
3. GDP at market prices equals GDP at factor cost minus net indirect taxes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: GNP adds net factor income from abroad to GDP, and NNP at factor cost is national income. Market price includes indirect taxes less subsidies, so GDP at market price equals GDP at factor cost plus net indirect taxes, making statement 3 wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, National Income

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Borrowings are treated as non-debt receipts while computing the fiscal deficit.
2. Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
3. Primary deficit is the fiscal deficit minus interest payments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fiscal deficit measures the total borrowing need, so borrowings are excluded from receipts. Revenue deficit and primary deficit are defined as in statements 2 and 3.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Fiscal Policy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Narrow money (M1) includes the time deposits of commercial banks.
2. Reserve money is also known as high-powered money.
3. Broad money (M3) includes the time deposits of banks.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Reserve money is the base on which banks create deposits, hence 'high-powered'. M3 is M1 plus time deposits with banks, so time deposits belong to broad money and not to narrow money M1.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Money and Banking

questions.q: Core inflation is a measure of inflation that excludes which of the following components?
questions.e: Food and fuel prices swing with weather and global shocks, so removing them reveals the underlying demand-led trend. This is why policymakers watch core inflation to judge whether price pressure is persistent.

questions.q:
Statement-I: An increase in the Cash Reserve Ratio reduces the lending capacity of commercial banks.
Statement-II: The Cash Reserve Ratio is the share of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that must be kept with the Reserve Bank of India.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A higher CRR means more of every deposit is locked with the RBI, leaving less money to lend. That is why raising CRR is a tool to absorb liquidity and curb credit expansion.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Money and Banking

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT recorded in the current account of India's Balance of Payments?
o: Remittances sent by Indians working abroad
questions.e: Foreign portfolio investment is a capital (financial) account flow. Trade in goods, remittances (secondary income) and interest payments (primary income) are all current account items.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, External Sector

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Yellow Revolution : Oilseeds production
2. White Revolution : Foodgrain production
3. Blue Revolution : Fish production
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Yellow Revolution aimed at oilseeds and the Blue Revolution at fisheries. The White Revolution (Operation Flood, Verghese Kurien) was about milk, not foodgrains, so pair 2 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT an instrument of the money market?
questions.e: The money market deals in short-term instruments of up to one year, such as Treasury Bills, commercial paper and certificates of deposit. Debentures are long-term debt and trade in the capital market.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy, Financial Markets

questions.q: Which one of the following ecological pyramids is never inverted in a natural ecosystem?
o: Both pyramid of numbers and pyramid of biomass
questions.e: Energy is lost at each trophic level through respiration and heat, so the energy pyramid is always upright. Numbers can be inverted (one tree, many insects) and biomass can be inverted in oceans, where small phytoplankton are consumed as fast as they grow.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Denitrification converts nitrates back into gaseous nitrogen.
2. The phosphorus cycle has a major gaseous phase in the atmosphere.
3. Nitrification is carried out by bacteria such as Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Denitrifying bacteria return nitrogen to the air, and Nitrosomonas then Nitrobacter oxidise ammonia to nitrite and nitrate. Phosphorus is a sedimentary cycle with rocks as the reservoir and no significant gaseous phase, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.q:
Which of the following are recognised as biodiversity hotspots that include parts of India?
1. Western Ghats and Sri Lanka
2. Indo-Burma
3. Eastern Ghats
4. Himalaya
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: India's hotspots are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma, the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (which includes the Nicobar Islands). The Eastern Ghats are not a recognised hotspot.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Project Tiger was launched in 1983.
2. Project Elephant was launched in 1992.
3. The National Tiger Conservation Authority is chaired by the Union Minister in charge of Environment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Project Elephant began in 1992 and the NTCA, a statutory body under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, is chaired by the Environment Minister. Project Tiger was launched earlier, in 1973, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following international conventions aims to eliminate or restrict the production and use of Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)?
questions.e: The Stockholm Convention targets POPs such as DDT, PCBs and dioxins, which persist and bioaccumulate. Rotterdam concerns prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals, Basel concerns hazardous waste movement, and Minamata concerns mercury.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Over a 100-year period, methane has a higher global warming potential than carbon dioxide.
2. The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in 1997.
3. Under the Paris Agreement, only developed countries are required to submit Nationally Determined Contributions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Methane traps far more heat per tonne than CO2, though it stays in the atmosphere for a shorter time, and the Kyoto Protocol dates from 1997. The Paris Agreement asks all parties, not just developed ones, to submit NDCs, which is its key difference from Kyoto.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Normal unpolluted rain is slightly acidic, and rain is generally called acid rain when its pH falls below 5.6.
Statement-II: Acid rain is caused mainly by emissions of carbon dioxide.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Dissolved atmospheric CO2 makes natural rain mildly acidic, with a pH of about 5.6. Acid rain is caused chiefly by sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen, which form sulphuric and nitric acids, so statement II is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sound travels faster in solids than in gases.
2. Light travels faster in a denser medium than in a rarer medium.
3. The speed of sound in air increases with a rise in temperature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Closely packed particles in solids pass vibrations quickly, and warmer air has faster-moving molecules, so sound speeds up. Light slows down in a denser medium (refractive index above 1), so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class IX Science, Sound; Class X, Light

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sun-synchronous satellites are launched into equatorial orbits.
2. A geostationary satellite appears fixed in the sky because its orbital period equals the Earth's rotation period.
3. A geostationary orbit lies at an altitude of about 36,000 km above the equator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A geostationary satellite matches the Earth's rotation and sits above the equator at about 36,000 km, so it appears fixed. Sun-synchronous satellites are placed in near-polar orbits so that they pass over a place at the same local solar time, so statement 1 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-2 soft-landed successfully on the Moon in 2019.
2. India's Mars Orbiter Mission was launched by a GSLV rocket.
3. Chandrayaan-3 soft-landed near the lunar south polar region in August 2023.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land near the lunar south polar region. Vikram of Chandrayaan-2 crashed during descent, and the Mars Orbiter Mission was launched on a PSLV (PSLV-C25) in 2013.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chandrasekhar limit is about 1.4 times the mass of the Sun.
2. Pulsars are rapidly rotating neutron stars.
3. The Sun will end its life as a neutron star.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Chandrasekhar limit is the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf, and pulsars are neutron stars emitting beams that sweep past us. The Sun is far too light to become a neutron star and will end as a white dwarf.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Physics / Standard astronomy texts

questions.q: In a nuclear reactor, what is the function of a moderator?
o: To absorb excess neutrons and stop the chain reaction
To carry heat away from the reactor core
questions.e: Fast neutrons released in fission are poorly absorbed by uranium-235, so a moderator such as heavy water or graphite slows them to make the chain reaction sustainable. Control rods, coolants and fertile material (U-238) play the other roles named.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Polymerase Chain Reaction amplifies specific DNA segments using a heat-stable DNA polymerase.
2. Restriction endonucleases cut DNA at specific recognition sequences.
3. The CRISPR-Cas9 system primarily cuts RNA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PCR uses Taq polymerase, which survives the heating cycles, and restriction enzymes recognise particular DNA sequences. Cas9 is guided by RNA but cuts double-stranded DNA, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Biology, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In India, a registered Geographical Indication is valid for 10 years and can be renewed.
2. Under the Copyright Act, 1957, literary works are protected for the life of the author plus 50 years.
3. The term of a patent in India is 20 years from the date of filing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: GI registration lasts 10 years with renewal, and patents last 20 years from filing. Indian copyright for literary works runs for the author's life plus 60 years, not 50, so statement 2 is wrong.
